brief.greeting: Good morning. You’ll find more Indian law questions than coffee beans in tonight’s AI feed.

stories.headline: IndicIPR-QA covers Indian IPR laws
stories.body: **New legal QA benchmark:** IndicIPR-QA offers 4,462 extractive question‑answer pairs drawn from 1,116 statutory contexts across seven Indian IPR Acts.
stories.why: It gives you a ready‑made dataset for testing retrieval or LLM grounding on niche legal text.

stories.headline: Kernel cells propose unified container objects
stories.body: **Kernel rethink:** Josef Bacik suggests treating containers as first‑class "cells" to simplify container primitives inside the Linux kernel.
stories.why: A unified abstraction could reduce code duplication and make future container features easier to add.

stories.headline: Homebrewed SLMs train Portuguese models on a laptop
stories.body: **DIY language models:** A new tutorial ships a Python package and notebooks to train 11‑12 M‑parameter Portuguese models on a single consumer GPU, using both autoregressive and masked diffusion techniques.
stories.why: You can experiment with local LLMs without a cloud budget, perfect for rapid prototyping.

quick_hits.text: **Calibration:** RMC isolates newly memorized data in diffusion models for near‑perfect membership inference.
**Misalignment monitoring:** OpenAI layers checks to catch rogue behavior in frontier models early.
**Consensus math:** h‑Majority reaches agreement in ~√n/h rounds, tightening time‑sample trade‑offs.
**Agent runtime:** Rust’s infinity library adds principled concurrency for AI agents.

brief.sign_off: That’s your two‑minute briefing—see you tomorrow, code wizard .

highlights.title: IndicIPR-QA: A Benchmark for Extractive Question Answering on Indian IPR Laws
highlights.summary: IndicIPR-QA is an extractive QA benchmark covering all seven Indian IPR Acts with 4,462 question‑answer pairs drawn from 1,116 statutory contexts.
highlights.detail: The dataset was generated using GPT‑4o and passed nine automatic quality checks, multiple LLM evaluations, and a human audit of 200 pairs. Section-level partitioning ensures no source‑context overlap between train, validation, and test splits, improving robustness for low‑resource legal QA research.

highlights.title: Difficulty Calibration Across Time for Membership Inference in Diffusion Models
highlights.summary: Reference‑Model Calibration (RMC) compares a fine‑tuned diffusion model's loss to an earlier checkpoint, isolating newly memorized data and achieving near‑perfect membership inference auditing.
highlights.detail: RMC calibrates difficulty along both training time and diffusion time, addressing the problem where easy‑to‑reconstruct non‑members can receive lower loss than complex training images. By anchoring loss to a reference model, it separates memorization from inherent image difficulty, improving audit reliability without needing additional data.

highlights.title: Homebrewed SLMs: Autoregressive and Masked Diffusion Language Models Built at Home for Portuguese
highlights.summary: The Homebrewed SLMs tutorial releases a Python package and two notebooks for training Brazilian Portuguese language models of 11‑12 M parameters on a single consumer GPU.
highlights.detail: The guide includes tokenizer creation, a preregistered comparison protocol, and legal‑task benchmarks using Kneser‑Ney baselines. Autoregressive training peaks at 64 epochs before memorising the corpus, while masked diffusion continues improving up to 256 epochs, offering a practical baseline for domain‑specific Portuguese NLP.

highlights.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
highlights.summary: OpenAI employs layered monitoring to spot misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior in frontier models, enabling early intervention before incidents escalate.
highlights.detail: The monitoring stack combines automated checks, human oversight, and response protocols to detect deviations from intended behavior. This approach aims to mitigate risks associated with increasingly capable AI systems by providing multiple safety nets.

items.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
items.summary: OpenAI’s updated Model Spec defines five core values to guide the development of more capable and beneficial AI systems.
items.detail: The specification emphasizes sound judgment, respect for human agency, and fidelity to human intent, aiming to align future models with ethical and safety standards. It serves as a governance framework for internal and external AI development.

items.title: Catching Bugs Before They Land: JiTTesting’s Human-on-the-Loop Approach at Full Scale
items.summary: Meta has deployed its Just-in-Time Test generation (JiTTests) system in production, reporting positive impact on bug detection before code lands.
items.detail: The approach combines large language models with a human‑on‑the‑loop workflow to generate tests on the fly. Meta’s accompanying paper details the methodology and results. This marks a shift from post‑commit testing to proactive, on‑the‑fly verification.

items.title: How Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence
items.summary: Ropes & Gray is building an AI‑assisted transactional diligence platform in partnership with OpenAI, where lawyers review AI‑generated document groupings, summaries, and reports.
items.detail: The system aims to streamline the review of large document sets during deals, reducing manual effort while keeping lawyers in the loop for final advice. It reflects a growing trend of legal firms integrating generative AI into core workflows.

items.title: Granite Switch 4.1.1 — Update models like you update software
items.summary: Hugging Face announced Granite Switch version 4.1.1, enabling model updates to be applied like software patches.
items.detail: The release focuses on simplifying model lifecycle management, allowing developers to push incremental improvements without redeploying entire models. It aligns with broader efforts to treat ML models as mutable artifacts.

items.title: Model: mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B
items.summary: The Mistral‑Large‑4‑1T‑A52B model on Hugging Face has been downloaded 278 times and received 1,259 likes.
items.detail: The model supports image‑text‑to‑text tasks and is part of the trending list on the platform, indicating community interest despite its relatively low download count compared with larger models.

items.title: [$] Containers as a recognized kernel object
items.summary: Kernel developer Josef Bacik proposes "cells" as a first‑class kernel object to unify container primitives.
items.detail: Current Linux kernels expose namespaces, cgroups, and other mechanisms separately, requiring manual assembly for containers. The "cells" concept aims to provide a single abstraction, potentially simplifying container implementation and management.

items.title: Putting a MiSTer Marquee on a Better Display
items.summary: Hackaday details how to add a secondary marquee display to a MiSTer FPGA board to show core and game information.
items.detail: The guide walks through hardware selection, wiring, and firmware configuration, offering a low‑cost way to enhance the user interface of the retro‑gaming platform.

items.title: Security updates for Thursday
items.summary: Security updates were released on Thursday for AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Red Hat, and SUSE, covering dozens of packages such as kernel, gcc-toolset-15, Java 17/25, Firefox, and Thunderbird.
items.detail: The updates address vulnerabilities across core system components, development tools, and user applications. Each distribution lists a specific set of affected packages, indicating a coordinated effort to patch known issues promptly. Administrators should apply the updates to maintain system integrity.

items.title: 2026 Hackaday Supercon: All the Speakers!
items.summary: Hackaday announced the first round of speakers for the 2026 Hackaday Supercon conference.
items.detail: The speaker lineup includes experts from hardware hacking, open‑source firmware, and embedded design, setting the tone for the event's technical focus. Additional speakers and workshop details will be released incrementally as confirmations are secured.

items.title: An Attempt at a Useful Desktop OS For Microcontrollers
items.summary: Hackaday introduced a new desktop‑class operating system that can run directly on modern microcontrollers in 2026.
items.detail: The OS leverages recent MCU performance gains to provide a graphical interface and multitasking capabilities previously limited to full computers. It aims to simplify development by offering familiar desktop abstractions on low‑power hardware.

items.title: Is This The Only Instrument You Need?
items.summary: Hackaday argues that a single multifunction instrument can replace multiple separate tools like logic analyzers and oscilloscopes for many electronics projects.
items.detail: The article evaluates trade‑offs in functionality, cost, and portability, highlighting how integrated devices can streamline debugging while noting limitations in bandwidth and channel count compared to dedicated equipment.

items.title: Nearly-Optimal Time-Sample Trade-off in Consensus Dynamics
items.summary: The paper proves that h‑Majority consensus reaches agreement in roughly O~(sqrt(n)/h) rounds for any h ≥ 3, achieving a near‑optimal sample‑size versus time trade‑off.
items.detail: The analysis covers synchronous rounds where each node samples h peers uniformly with replacement and adopts the majority opinion. Results hold for any initial opinion distribution, with the bound improving as h grows, matching known lower limits for this class of dynamics.

items.title: Tessera: Fast Join-Aggregates over Skewed Sparse Relations in Database Engines
items.summary: Tessera is a skew‑aware join‑aggregate operator that directly computes sparse matrix products, avoiding materialization of billions of intermediate rows.
items.detail: By pruning values that cannot meet query thresholds and emitting only non‑zero result cells, Tessera reduces query runtimes from minutes to seconds on typical skewed datasets. It integrates into existing database engines without requiring external matrix libraries.

items.title: Rebuilding a Field's Open-Problem Catalog from the Literature: A Two-Layer Knowledge Graph, and Why Status Must Stay Proposed
items.summary: A two‑layer knowledge graph stores 1,053 database‑research and 1,000 AI‑research open problems as data, with a language model handling extraction, grounding, status verdicts, and idea generation.
items.detail: The system links a hand‑curated problem layer to an evidence layer rebuilt from a bibliographic index, using typed, provenance‑carrying edges in a single graph database. The language model is constrained to a candidate set, refusing out‑of‑set answers. This enables queries about current work on a problem or recent resolutions without manual survey updates.

items.title: Rimuru: Unified Memory Management for Modern LLM Serving via Elastic Expert Offloading
items.summary: Rimuru introduces unified memory management for LLM serving, allowing elastic offloading of expert tensors between weight and attention memory pools.
items.detail: Current serving stacks allocate fixed regions for model weights and attention states, leading to under‑utilization or bottlenecks as workload intensity changes. Rimuru’s approach pools heterogeneous tensors and dynamically reallocates memory based on runtime demand, handling varied tensor layouts and lifetimes without sacrificing performance.

items.title: SeQUeNCe.DQC: Full-stack Simulation of Distributed Quantum Computing
items.summary: SeQUeNCe.DQC adds full‑stack distributed‑quantum‑computing simulation, reproducing a two‑node trapped‑ion Grover experiment with a 71% success‑probability benchmark.
items.detail: The new module compiles monolithic circuits into topology‑aware execution plans and coordinates them via SeQUeNCe’s networking stack. Experiments show hybrid TeleGate/TeleData strategies can outperform pure gate‑teleportation, and the simulator captures physical overheads of distributed quantum processing.

items.title: Enabling Dynamic Resource Scaling in Quantum Circuit Simulations
items.summary: A Dynamic Management of Resources framework makes the QuEST state‑vector simulator malleable, allowing a single HPC job to resize between circuits of varying qubit counts.
items.detail: Because no state vector persists between circuits, resizing incurs no data redistribution and requires only a checkpoint of the next circuit index. This eliminates idle nodes from over‑provisioned jobs and reduces scheduler overhead from launching separate jobs per circuit.

items.title: hydro-project/infinity
items.summary: hydro‑project/infinity is a Rust library providing an agent runtime and tool protocol for principled agent concurrency.
items.detail: The project defines a lightweight protocol enabling agents to coordinate tool usage and manage concurrent execution safely, targeting applications that require reliable multi‑agent orchestration.

items.title: obra/superpowers
items.summary: obra/superpowers offers an agentic skills framework and software‑development methodology designed to structure and streamline development work.
items.detail: The framework codifies skill definitions and composable workflows, aiming to make agent‑driven development more predictable and maintainable across teams.

items.title: ros-navigation/navigation2
items.summary: ROS 2 Navigation provides a modular framework and system for robot navigation in the ROS 2 ecosystem.
items.detail: It includes planners, controllers, and recovery behaviors that can be swapped at runtime. The package is written in C++ and follows ROS 2 conventions, making it suitable for integration with other ROS 2 components.

items.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot
items.summary: CopilotKit/OpenBot offers open-source AI coworkers, each with an isolated browser, file system, and toolset, executing actions pre‑recorded for reproducibility.
items.detail: Agents can be programmed to perform tasks autonomously and their interactions are logged for debugging. The platform aims to simplify building multi‑agent AI workflows without custom infrastructure.

items.title: Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios
items.summary: Claude-Code-Game-Studios turns Claude Code into a full game development studio with a hierarchy of AI agents.
items.detail: The system models real studio roles, coordinating agents to handle tasks like asset creation, scripting, and testing. It demonstrates how large language model agents can be organized for complex creative pipelines.

items.title: NVIDIA/cuda-rust
items.summary: NVIDIA/cuda-rust provides Rust bindings and idiomatic abstractions for NVIDIA's CUDA platform, including host runtime crates and kernel programming models.
items.detail: It includes Tile (cutile-rs) for tile‑based computation and SIMT (cuda-oxide) for traditional CUDA kernels, enabling Rust developers to write GPU code with safety guarantees.
